subject: Switchability score & price bridge proposal for Langwell
messages:
From: Ellie Park <ellie@langwell.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@langwell.ai, Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@cloudops.co>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — can Redwood match BlueFrame & migration credits?

Hi Sofia,

We ran a head-to-head on inference economics and BlueFrame has presented a pretty aggressive retention package for us (volume-based discounts + a 3-month migration credit). Our execs have asked if Redwood can match on price/credits and also provide a candid assessment of the technical lift to move our production pipelines (batch and streaming inference) over in Q3.

Key items:
- Current run-rate: ~15M token-gen / month, mostly API call driven with bursts.
- BlueFrame quoted: $0.0008/token gen (post-discount), 3 months of free usage (capped at 20M tokens).
- They included a one-page migration runbook and an SLA carve-out for zero-downtime migration.

Can you send over a price-bridge (match or near-match) and an estimate of switchability risk — i.e., how much custom engineering we should budget? If you can include a suggested migration credit structure and any required contract caveats, that would be helpful.

Thanks — we need something to present internally by next Tuesday.

Ellie
Ellie Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Langwell AI

Attachment: BlueFrame_offer_summary.pdf (external vendor stub)

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Team — forwarding Langwell's ask. They want a price match + credible migration incentive and a clear sense of technical effort. Quick thoughts:

1) Can we compute a switchability score (0-10) that summarizes integration risk — runtime compatibility, KV cache diff, tokenization edge cases, and infra ops?
2) Marcus — can you draft a competitive bridge with concrete numbers (discounted token price, migration credit structure, timeline-limited offer)?
3) Jonas — need a short tech summary we can share (weeks to migrate, major blockers, recommended pilot cadence).

Goal: get a short deliverable to Ellie by Monday EOD Pacific. Keeping it conservative is fine — we can include options (match exactly vs value-add credits).

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.ai

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick ask — can Redwood match BlueFrame & migration credits?

Quick technical read:

Switchability score (0 = high risk, 10 = trivial): 7/10. Rationale:
- Runtime compatibility: Langwell uses standard transformer stacks and a mix of long-context requests (~2–5% > 2k tokens). Our serving runtime supports that with minor config changes.
- KV cache: they rely on session affinity and prefix caching; we support transparent KV caching but may need a short workback to align TTL semantics — low effort (~1 week).
- Tokenization/decoding: likely minor tokenization diffs on a few prompt templates — estimate 2–3 dev-days for QA.
- Ops/instrumentation: they want per-route latency and token-level billing traces — we already have that in console; onboarding of their dashboards adds ~3–4 dev-days.

Suggested migration approach:
- 2-week pilot on a throttled subset (10% traffic) to validate outputs and latency.
- 4-week parallel run to measure cost and tune batching/quantization profiles.
- Final cutover with canary + rollback window (48 hours).

Estimated engineering hours (Redwood + Langwell collaboration): 80–120 hours total. Major unknowns: any proprietary tokenization hooks or model variants they keep internally.

I will prepare a one-page "switchability matrix" (attached) mapping each risk to mitigation steps.

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: switchability-score-matrix.xlsx (technical matrix)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jul 2025 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick ask — can Redwood match BlueFrame & migration credits?

Pricing options (draft):

Baseline (no credits):
- List token-gen rate: $0.0011/token gen
- Proposed enterprise discount for Langwell (based on 15M/mo): 20% => $0.00088/token gen

Match option (to mirror BlueFrame):
- Promotional discounted rate: $0.00080/token gen for first 6 months (volume commitment: 12 months, expect step-down after 6mo)
- Migration credit: upfront usage credit of 20M tokens (applies to first 3 months)

Value-add alternative (we differentiate on ops & quality):
- Offer $0.0009/token gen + 2 months migration credit capped at 15M tokens + dedicated migration support (SWE hours + runbook alignment)
- Include 30-day cost-smoothing clause: if monthly usage spikes >20%, credits auto-adjust pro-rata to avoid bill shock.

Commercial caveats:
- Migration credits are consumption credits, not refundable cash.
- SLA and uptime addendum: we can offer a 99.9% SLA for production routes once dedicated routing is in place (requires reserved capacity or dedicated pool).

Recommendation: present the Match option as an "Escalation Offer" that requires a 12-month minimum commitment and a signed addendum for the migration credits (to avoid gaming). Alternatively, the Value-add option is a lower discount with clearer operational guarantees.

I'll draft a clean term sheet (2 pages) and the credit mechanics. Marcus
Marcus Lin
Commercial Operations Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Langwell_Redwood_Termsheet_v1.pdf (pricing sheet stub)

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Ellie Park <ellie@langwell.ai>, procurement@langwell.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 27 Jul 2025 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed bridge: Langwell offer and migration plan (two options)

Hi Ellie & team — thanks for the clarity in your original note. Attached are two concise options for internal review (term sheet + technical switchability matrix + a brief migration runbook):

1) Match Option (time-limited escalation)
- Rate: $0.00080/token gen for first 6 months (applies to token generation only)
- Migration credit: 20M tokens applied to the first 3 months
- Requirements: 12-month minimum commitment; DocuSign addendum to lock credit mechanics
- Support: prioritised onboarding queue and a dedicated solutions engineer during pilot

2) Differentiated Value Option
- Rate: $0.00090/token gen for first 6 months
- Migration credit: 15M tokens over first 2 months
- Support: dedicated migration bundle (10 SWE-hours included) + cost smoothing clause
- SLA: 99.9% with reserved capacity add-on (optional)

Technical read: Jonas attached a switchability matrix — we estimate a 6-week end-to-end migration window using a pilot -> parallel run -> canary cutover cadence. Total collaboration hours ~80–120. Major caveat: if Langwell requires nonstandard tokenizers or private model variants, estimate may increase.

Next step: let us know which option you prefer and we will deliver a one-page addendum for signature. If you want to expedite the Match Option we can push the DocuSign and an initial pilot kickoff within 7 business days of signature.

Attachments: Langwell_Redwood_Termsheet_v1.pdf, switchability-score-matrix.xlsx, migration-runbook-draft.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-minute call if that helps.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
